dependent_variable.name: CONACCi
dependent_variable.definition: Accrual-based conservatism proxy: the negative of the six-year mean of total accruals before depreciation, scaled by assets. Total accruals before depreciation are net income before extraordinary items plus depreciation expense less operating cash flows.
dependent_variable.formula: CONACCi = −mean_{1993–1998}[(NI before extraordinary items + depreciation expense − operating cash flows) / assets].

evidence.quote: Specifically, we use the sum of total accruals excluding depreciation (net income before extraordinary items plus depreciation expense less operating cash flows) deflated by assets and averaged within each of the two sample periods, 1993–1998 and 1987–1992, respectively, as our accrual-based proxy for conservatism.
We also multiply this measure by –1 so it is increasing in the amount of negative accruals, and refer to it as CONACC.

dependent_variable.definition: Book-to-market ratio for firm i at fiscal year-end t.

evidence.quote: the book-to-market ratio for firm i at fiscal year-end t;

independent_variables.name: RET_i,t
independent_variables.definition: Stock return (with dividends) for firm i at fiscal year t−k.

evidence.quote: BTM_it = alpha + alpha_i + alpha_t + sum_k=0^6 beta_k*RET_i,t-k + e_it. This has seven return regressors: RET_it, RET_i,t-1, RET_i,t-2, RET_i,t-3, RET_i,t-4, RET_i,t-5, RET_i,t-6. Alpha is a common intercept; alpha_i is the firm-specific component and alpha_t the time-specific component. The source says the firm-specific coefficient alpha_i is used to measure conservatism.
